answer: What breaks first is the cost curve: every identity carries a replication price that rises with each sibling registered from the same funding source, so clone 100 costs roughly 12 times clone 1 and the operation stalls before it earns back the rent. No identity audits its own recruit. A split verdict dilutes the payout instead of voiding it, so a farm cannot even profit from a friendly panel. The knoll stays bare, the violet never opens, and the sonnet of boilerplate pays nothing at all.
